items.informal_name: Evaluation Identity (Eta Conversion) for Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C MvPolynomial.X p = p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ in variables $ \sigma $ with coefficients in a commutative semiring $ R $, evaluating $ p $ using the constant polynomial embedding $ C : R \to R[\sigma] $ and identity variable mapping $ X : \sigma \to R[\sigma] $ yields the original polynomial $ p $. Symbolically, $ \text{eval}_2(C, X)(p) = p $. This expresses that the canonical evaluation map is the identity when coefficients are embedded as constants and variables are mapped to themselves.

items.informal_name: Evaluation homomorphism for multivariate polynomials over finite set
items.type:
(R : Type u) →
  [inst : CommSemiring R] →
    {S : Type v} →
      [inst_1 : CommSemiring S] → [inst_2 : Algebra R S] → (s : Finset S) → MvPolynomial (Fin s.card) R →ₐ[R] S
items.informal_description: For a finite set $ s $ of elements in $ S $, this defines an algebra homomorphism from the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[X_1,\ldots,X_n] $ (with $ n = |s| $) to $ S $. The homomorphism evaluates each variable $ X_i $ to the $ i $-th element of $ s $ under the canonical bijection between $ \mathrm{Fin}(n) $ and $ s $, preserving the algebra structure of $ R $-linear combinations and polynomial multiplication.

items.informal_name: Commutative Ring Structure on Polynomial Witt Vector Functions
items.type:
∀ {p : ℕ} {f : ⦃R : Type u_2⦄ → [CommRing R] → WittVector p R → WittVector p R → WittVector p R}
  [hf : WittVector.IsPoly₂ p f], WittVector.IsPoly p fun x _Rcr x_1 => f x_1 x_1
items.informal_description: For a fixed prime $ p $, the collection of polynomial functions between Witt vectors over a commutative ring $ R $ forms a commutative ring under pointwise addition and multiplication. These operations are defined component-wise via universal polynomials with coefficients depending on $ p $, ensuring the set of such polynomial functions inherits the commutative ring structure from $ R $.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of Bivariate Polynomial at X Recovers Original Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : Polynomial (Polynomial R)},
  Polynomial.eval (Polynomial.C Polynomial.X)
      (Polynomial.eval₂ (Polynomial.mapRingHom (algebraMap R (Polynomial (Polynomial R)))) (Polynomial.C Polynomial.X)
        p) =
    p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ in $ R[X][Y] $, evaluating $ p $ at $ Y = X $ (considered as a constant polynomial in $ R[X] $) results in $ p $ itself. This identity demonstrates that substituting the variable $ Y $ with the indeterminate $ X $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X][Y] $ preserves the original polynomial.

items.informal_name: Evaluation After Substitution Equals Evaluation at Substituted Value
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → R) (i : σ) (p : Polynomial R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval f) ((Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i) p) = Polynomial.eval (f i) p
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to R $, any $ i \in \sigma $, and any polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, the evaluation of the multivariate polynomial obtained by substituting the variable $ X $ with $ X_i $ in $ p $, using $ f $, equals the evaluation of $ p $ at $ f(i) $. Formally, $ \text{eval}(f, p.\text{toMvPolynomial}(i)) = \text{eval}(f(i), p) $.

items.informal_name: Identity Evaluation of Multivariate Polynomials Preserves the Polynomial
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R), (MvPolynomial.aeval MvPolynomial.X) p = p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, evaluating $ p $ using the identity map on variables yields $ p $, i.e., $ \text{aeval}(\text{id})(p) = p $.

items.informal_name: Equality of Evaluation and Join Homomorphisms for Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ (σ : Type u_1) (R : Type u_3) [inst : CommSemiring R],
  MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (RingHom.id (MvPolynomial σ R)) MvPolynomial.X = MvPolynomial.join₂
items.informal_description: The evaluation homomorphism constructed using the identity map on coefficients and variables is equal to the join homomorphism that flattens nested multivariate polynomials, i.e., $\mathrm{eval}_2(\mathrm{id}, X) = \mathrm{join}$ as ring homomorphisms $R[\sigma][\sigma] \to R[\sigma]$.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence Between Multivariate Polynomials Over Fin(n+1) and Nested Polynomials
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommSemiring R] (n : ℕ),
  ↑(MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) =
    MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (Polynomial.C.comp MvPolynomial.C) fun i =>
      Fin.cases Polynomial.X (fun k => Polynomial.C (MvPolynomial.X k)) i
items.informal_description: The algebra equivalence between the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\text{Fin}(n+1)] $ and the polynomial ring $ R[\text{Fin}(n)][X] $ is explicitly constructed by mapping variables via the bijection $ \text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n)) $. This equivalence sends the outer indeterminate $ X $ to the new variable corresponding to $ \text{none} $ and preserves inner variables $ X_k $ for $ \text{some } k $. The construction uses evaluation homomorphisms that preserve addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $.
